title: AP CSP — Lesson 25 Homework: Redundancy & Fault Tolerance
notice: All questions are original. Q1–Q6 are AP-style practice, not official or past AP questions. Q7–Q12 are classroom written responses, not official exam FRQs. The 30 marks are teacher-assigned. For Q5 select exactly TWO answers; its one mark requires both correct choices and no others. Follow AP pseudocode semantics.

questions.prompt: What is redundancy in a system?

options.label: A
options.text: A promise that nothing fails

options.label: B
options.text: Extra components that can mitigate other failures

options.label: C
options.text: The removal of all alternative paths

options.label: D
options.text: A larger font on a network map

questions.explanation: B describes useful alternatives. A overclaims; C reduces redundancy; D changes only presentation.

questions.prompt: Which observation demonstrates fault tolerance for S-to-T communication?

options.label: A
options.text: No component has ever failed.

options.label: B
options.text: A diagram has many colors.

options.label: C
options.text: Communication continues after a specified link fails.

options.label: D
options.text: The receiver’s software never needs testing.

questions.explanation: C ties a failure to a maintained function. A observes no fault; B is cosmetic; D invents immunity for software.

questions.prompt: S-A-C-T loses A-C. Working edges S-A, A-D, D-T remain. Which path works?

options.label: A
options.text: S-A-D-T

options.label: B
options.text: S-A-C-T

options.label: C
options.text: S-T, even without that edge

options.label: D
options.text: S-C-T, even without S-C

questions.explanation: A uses the stated working edges. B uses failed A-C; C and D invent absent links.

questions.prompt: S has only two incident links, S-A and S-B. Both fail. What follows?

options.label: A
options.text: Remote extra links automatically reconnect S.

options.label: B
options.text: S can jump to T.

options.label: C
options.text: Only bandwidth changes.

options.label: D
options.text: S cannot reach any other node.

questions.explanation: D follows from no working first link. A and B invent connectivity; C ignores complete isolation.

options.label: A
options.text: Redundancy may require more equipment or maintenance.

options.label: B
options.text: Any two drawn routes fail independently.

options.label: C
options.text: A path guarantees a functioning application.

options.label: D
options.text: Multiple routes can share a physical failure risk.

questions.explanation: A states a resource cost. D recognizes shared infrastructure. B assumes independence from a diagram; C overclaims end-to-end service. Select A and D only.

questions.prompt: Route X has 3 hops and route Y has 4. What can be concluded about real delay from this alone?

options.label: A
options.text: Y is always slower by 1 second.

options.label: B
options.text: Actual delay is not determined by hop count alone.

options.label: C
options.text: Both have the same bandwidth.

options.label: D
options.text: X can never lose packets.

questions.explanation: B respects missing link/waiting information. A invents timing units; C invents capacity; D invents delivery reliability.

questions.prompt: All edges are undirected: S-A, S-B, A-C, A-D, B-D, C-T, D-T, C-D. (a) Give two different S-to-T paths, including one avoiding A-C. (b) Give each hop count. (c) Explain how those alternatives help if A-C fails.
questions.answer: Examples S-A-C-T and S-B-D-T, each 3 hops. The second avoids A-C and remains usable.
questions.explanation: Examples S-A-C-T and S-B-D-T, each 3 hops. The second avoids A-C and remains usable.

rubric.criterion: Gives one valid S-to-T path.
Gives a different valid path.
Correctly counts hops for both.
Identifies a stated route avoiding failed A-C.

questions.prompt: Use the graph in Q7. Only C-D fails. (a) Give a working route. (b) Count its hops. (c) Does S-A-C-T remain valid? Explain. (d) Does unchanged routing mean the failed edge did not exist?
questions.answer: S-A-C-T; 3 hops; it uses none of C-D; no, the failure can affect alternatives without changing this route.
questions.explanation: S-A-C-T; 3 hops; it uses none of C-D; no, the failure can affect alternatives without changing this route.

rubric.criterion: Gives a valid route avoiding C-D.
Correctly counts that route’s hops.
Explains S-A-C-T excludes C-D.
Distinguishes an unchanged selected path from absence of a failed component.

questions.prompt: Use Q7’s graph. Disable C-T and D-T together. (a) Is S-to-T communication possible? (b) Explain structurally. (c) Give a different two-edge set that also disconnects S and T. (d) Explain why extra edges elsewhere are insufficient.
questions.answer: No; T has no working incident links. S-A and S-B is another disconnecting set. A route cannot start/end across a missing local connection.
questions.explanation: No; T has no working incident links. S-A and S-B is another disconnecting set. A route cannot start/end across a missing local connection.

rubric.criterion: States no S-to-T path.
Identifies isolation of T.
Gives S-A and S-B as a valid alternative set.
Explains that remote edges cannot repair the isolated endpoint connection.

questions.prompt: Use Q7’s graph. Disable S-B, A-D and C-T. (a) Give the surviving S-to-T route. (b) Count hops. (c) At exactly 1 time unit per hop, give its cost. (d) Why is this not a measured Internet delay?
questions.answer: S-A-C-D-T; 4 hops; 4 units; the equal-hop cost is an assumption and real links/queues differ.
questions.explanation: S-A-C-D-T; 4 hops; 4 units; the equal-hop cost is an assumption and real links/queues differ.

rubric.criterion: Gives S-A-C-D-T.
Counts four hops.
Calculates four stated time units.
Identifies the timing assumption or omitted real delay factors.

questions.prompt: Two routes use cables in the same tunnel. (a) Identify a shared risk. (b) Explain why two drawn routes do not ensure independent failure. (c) Propose a relevant improvement. (d) Give one associated resource cost.
questions.answer: Tunnel damage could affect both. Logical alternatives share physical infrastructure. Use a physically separate route; this can require extra cable, equipment or maintenance.
questions.explanation: Tunnel damage could affect both. Logical alternatives share physical infrastructure. Use a physically separate route; this can require extra cable, equipment or maintenance.

rubric.criterion: Identifies a common tunnel-related failure.
Explains shared infrastructure connects their failure risk.
Proposes physical separation or another relevant independent alternative.
Names a plausible resource/maintenance cost.

questions.prompt: A team observes a route after one link failure and says the whole service can never fail. (a) State what their evidence supports. (b) Give a network counterexample using Q7. (c) Give a non-path limitation. (d) Rewrite the claim accurately.
questions.answer: It supports reachability for that tested failure. S-A and S-B together disconnect. A failed receiver/application can still prevent service. The tested link failure was tolerated for S-to-T reachability.
questions.explanation: It supports reachability for that tested failure. S-A and S-B together disconnect. A failed receiver/application can still prevent service. The tested link failure was tolerated for S-to-T reachability.

rubric.criterion: Limits evidence to the tested failure and communication function.
Gives a valid disconnecting failure set.
Identifies an endpoint/application or other omitted failure.
States a bounded claim rather than immunity.
